text: The first Government of Prime Minister Sali Berisha was the 63rd ruling Government of the Republic of Albania, established on 8 September 2005. After the 3 July 2005 election, the Democratic Party formed a center-right post-electoral alliance to secure a majority in Parliament and establish the government. This alliance, composed of five center-right parties led by Sali Berisha, achieved a majority of 81 deputies out of 140 in the Assembly. The new government was approved on 8 September with 84 votes in favor and officially took oath on 11 September in the presence of President of the Republic Alfred Moisiu. The table below outlines the ministers of the Berisha I government from the day of the oath, 11 September 2005, until its replacement on 17 September 2009. In 2007, Sokol Olldashi resigned to run in the local elections against Edi Rama for the Municipality of Tirana, leaving the position of Minister of Interior vacant for about two months. During this period, Deputy Minister Gjergj Lezhja temporarily assumed the ministerial functions, although the presidential decree dismissing Olldashi was published in March alongside other changes. In March of the same year, six ministers were replaced. In early May, a public conflict occurred between Prime Minister Sali Berisha and Minister of Foreign Affairs Besnik Mustafaj during a debate in the PM's office. Lulzim Basha was appointed to replace Mustafaj, having previously served as Minister of Public Works, Transport and Telecommunications. Subsequently, Sokol Olldashi was appointed to the position vacated by Basha.
